data.narrative:
Innoviz Technologies (INVZ) is a publicly traded company operating in the Drones & Autonomous sector. The valuation universe for comparable analysis is limited: five private peers operate in the sector (Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, Elroy Air), with no public peers identified in the same or adjacent stages. This narrow comp set reflects the early-stage, capital-intensive nature of autonomous vehicle development.

The Peer-Median triangulation method is not applicable to this valuation. The five same-sector peers identified do not satisfy the screening criteria requiring a minimum of three datapoints within consistent stage or valuation-tier bands. Applying all-sector medians would introduce material distortion given the heterogeneous risk profiles, technology maturity, and funding dynamics across Drones & Autonomous subsegments.

Without a sufficiently robust peer-median foundation, this analysis cannot reliably support a quantitative valuation range or narrow confidence intervals. The absence of public trading comparables and the inability to construct a tight peer subset means alternative methods—enterprise value to revenue/cash burn multiples, discounted cash flow analysis with disclosed unit economics, or forward transaction precedents—would be required to triangulate fair value. Key uncertainties include regulatory pathway clarity, path to positive unit economics, and capital intensity through commercialization. A complete valuation would require non-public financial data or alternative methodologies not available from the provided dataset.
